### LD score regression

LD Score Regression (LDSC) is run within each ancestry: heritability (h²) of each GWAS, and genetic correlation (rg) of **every pair** of GWAS of that ancestry (LDSC's own `--rg a,b,c` estimates only the first against the rest, so the pipeline runs it once per GWAS). LDSC is not run between ancestries: LD differs between populations, so cross-ancestry genetic correlation needs dedicated methods (e.g. Popcorn).

For binary traits the pipeline uses the effective sample size (`N_EFF`) and, when the population prevalence is given, reports liability-scale heritability (`H2_LIAB`, with a sample prevalence of 0.5 for effective N; Grotzinger et al. 2023). `H2_Z` is the z-score of the observed-scale heritability. A genetic correlation is flagged as unreliable (`RG_RELIABLE` FALSE) when either trait's `H2_Z` is below 4 or the estimate lies outside [-1, 1]; such estimates should not be interpreted. An intercept well above 1 for h² can indicate confounding or a sample size that is too large; "Ratio < 0" means the intercept is below 1, often from genomic-control-corrected input, which LDSC should not be given.

```{r echo = F}
ldsc_tables <- function(pattern) {
  files <- Sys.glob(paste0(params$ldsc_directory, pattern))
  tables <- lapply(files, function(f) data.table::fread(f))
  tables <- Filter(function(t) nrow(t) > 0, tables)
  if (length(tables) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.table::rbindlist(tables, fill = TRUE)
}
h2_table <- ldsc_tables("*_h2.tsv")
if (!is.null(h2_table)) {
  shown <- intersect(c("ANCESTRY", "TRAIT", "H2_OBS", "H2_OBS_SE", "H2_LIAB", "H2_LIAB_SE", "H2_Z", "INTERCEPT",
                       "INTERCEPT_SE", "RATIO", "MEAN_CHISQ", "FLAG_LOW_H2_Z", "RATIO_NOTE"), names(h2_table))
  knitr::kable(h2_table[, ..shown], digits = 4, caption = "Heritability")
}
```

```{r echo = F}
rg_table <- ldsc_tables("*_rg.tsv")
if (!is.null(rg_table)) {
  shown <- intersect(c("ANCESTRY", "TRAIT_1", "TRAIT_2", "RG", "RG_SE", "RG_P", "GCOV_INTERCEPT", "H2_Z_1",
                       "H2_Z_2", "RG_RELIABLE"), names(rg_table))
  knitr::kable(rg_table[, ..shown], digits = 4, caption = "Genetic correlation (every pair within ancestry)")
}
```

The full LDSC logs are in `r params$ldsc_directory`.

### Plots Comparing Heterogeneity Across Significant SNPs

The first plot shows the per-GWAS contribution to the Cochran's Q heterogeneity statistic for **all** clumped SNPs (one row per SNP). The second plot is a grouped forest plot of effect sizes for the **subset** of SNPs whose heterogeneity Q p-value passes Bonferroni correction (Q p-value < 0.05 / number of SNPs tested), i.e. only the significantly heterogeneous SNPs.

`r sprintf("![Per-GWAS contribution to heterogeneity Q-statistic (all clumped SNPs)](%s)", params$heterogeneity_plot)`
`r sprintf("![Forest plot of effect sizes for SNPs with significant heterogeneity (Bonferroni-corrected)](%s)", params$heterogeneity_snp_comparison)`

### Expected vs Observed Results

Compares the expected replication rate (based on discovery effect sizes and replication standard errors) against the observed replication rate across all GWAS pairs — a discrepancy suggests winner's curse or population differences.

```{r echo=F}
expected_vs_observed <- vroom::vroom(params$results, show_col_types = F)
knitr::kable(expected_vs_observed)
```
### Table of Heterogeneity Results

Per-SNP Cochran's Q p-values and per-GWAS contribution p-values (Qj) for all clumped SNPs tested for heterogeneity of effect sizes across the input GWAS.

```{r echo=F}
heterogeneity_results <- vroom::vroom(params$heterogeneity_scores, show_col_types = F)
knitr::kable(heterogeneity_results)
```
